title.narrative: Ecuador Disaster Risk Management Development Policy Financing with a Cat-DDO

description.narrative: The development objective of the Disaster Risk Management Development Policy Financing (DPF) with a Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option (Cat-DDO) for Ecuador is to strengthen the Government of Ecuador's program to manage risks resulting from climate, disaster, and public health shocks by: (i) enhancing institutional capacity, and (ii) mainstreaming resilience and climate adaptation in selected sectors. Ecuador has a solid legal framework for disaster and health crisis management, including clear institutional roles, a formal disaster declaration mechanism that serves as the trigger, and mandated tools such as national and local disaster risk management (DRM) plans and a disaster risk financing (DRF) strategy, all articulated in the 2024 DRM law and its regulations. The Cat-DDO builds on the progress and lessons learned from a series of DPF operations, Investment Project Financing (IPF), and non-lending technical assistance (TA) activities. This operation reinforces the Government of Ecuador (GoE's) ongoing efforts to strengthen institutional, technical, and financial capacities for managing disaster and climate change risks.

To strengthen the Government of Ecuador's program to manage risks resulting from climate, disaster, and public health shocks by (i) enhancing institutional capacity and (ii) mainstreaming resilience and climate adaptation in selected sectors.

title.narrative: Results indicator 1: Number of municipalities that have developed comprehensive risk management plans that include at least two measures focused on women reviewed by the SNGR

comment.narrative: PA1: Although no municipalities are currently counted under the indicator, SNGR has made significant progress in developing and piloting the methodological guide for Cantonal Comprehensive Climate and Disaster Risk Management Plans (PGIRCD-C). Since late 2025, pilot processes have been initiated in 10 cantons to validate and strengthen the methodology, including the integration of cross-cutting approaches such as gender, inclusion, and climate change adaptation. Pilot municipalities are currently advancing through the territorial diagnosis and plan development phases, with several municipalities showing substantial progress. The pilots have also identified opportunities to strengthen the methodology and improve alignment with other territorial planning instruments. As the pilots remain under technical adjustment, validation, and institutional review, none are yet counted toward achievement of the indicator, although progress remains on track.

title.narrative: Results indicator 3: Number of municipalities that have updated PDOTs incorporating DRM and climate adaptation in line with the Technical Standard reviewed by the SNGR

comment.narrative: PA3: Although no municipalities are currently counted under the indicator, the SNGR has initiated the compilation and systematization of Development and Land Use Plans (PDOTs) currently in force at the national level, in coordination with the Superintendence of Territorial Planning, Land Use and Management. This process will establish an official and validated baseline to support the application of SNGR's institutional methodology for assessing the integration of disaster risk management and climate change adaptation into PDOTs. While no municipalities are yet counted toward achievement of the indicator, implementation activities are progressing as planned.

title.narrative: Results indicator 5: Hectares of terrestrial and aquatic areas under enhanced conservation and management

comment.narrative: PA5: MAE reported progress in the number of hectares covered and committed to submitting the updated information to the World Bank by the end of May 2026. Progress has also been made in finalizing the Amazon Conservation Plan, which is scheduled for signing in August 2026. Once finalized, the Plan will be formally adopted through an administrative act, thereby fulfilling the Government's commitment related to the debt operation. Each protected area has an associated monitoring plan, specifically through the implementation of a SMART monitoring framework. The Bank team continues to follow up with counterparts to obtain the values for the results indicator.

Results indicator 4: Estimated capacity of distributed private renewable energy projects up to 100 MW approved by the MAE

comment.narrative: PA4: MAE reported progress on the results indicator, indicating that eight projects have received definitive feasibility approval from the Electricity Distribution Companies, in accordance with the established milestones (project identification, preliminary feasibility, qualification, and definitive feasibility). These projects represent a total installed capacity of 79.75 MW, equivalent to approximately 82.5 percent of the 2026 target (96.58 MW) and 40.6 percent of the final target for 2028 (196.518 MW). Based on the reported information, implementation progress remains on track.
